newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index edged up on Thursday in line with the domestic A share market, but trading was dull and little movement is expected before the bulk of 1996 company results are released, brokers said.
The B share index moved up 0.211 points or 0.29 percent to 73.276 points on volume of 10.2 million shares worth $4.8 million against $6.6 million on Wednesday.
The A share index rose 12.988 points or one percent to 1,305.726 points. Turnover was 7.9 billion yuan compared with Wednesday's eight billion yuan.
Brokers said that market sentiment was cautious before most company released their 1996 annual results.
China's listed firms are required to make public their 1996 results by the end of April, but only a handful of 43 B share companies listed in Shanghai have done so.
"Only a few domestic investors were seen trading while most institutions stayed on the sidelines with the company results unclear," one broker said.
"The market mood is still stable," a second broker said. "The index is likely to hit the 78-point level after the recent consolidation."
All 43 B shares traded, with 16 up, 11 flat and 16 up.
Shanghai Dazhong taxi was the star on a rebound after falls in the past few days, jumping $0.104 or 9.71 percent to $1.174 on volume of 281,000 shares.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device traded the most on institutional support, ending flat at $0.246 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index reversed morning losses on a bargain-hunting rush into the market in the afternoon on bullish sentiment, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 50.180 points or 1.47 percent to 3,467.606 points.
Shenyang Neu-Alpine Software was the biggest winner on institutional buying, surging 2.76 yuan or 10 percent to its daily limit-up of 30.36 yuan on volume of 3.0 million shares.
